### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `cfa24a3ace84f4bd2a96b604a572aee18c64193109bdcd5bd65e1a67560fe154`)

```text
/--
The trivial lower bound from Parseval's identity: for any polynomial $P$ of degree $n$ with
coefficients in $\{-1, 1\}$, we have $\max_{|z|=1} |P(z)| \geq \sqrt{n+1}$.

This follows from Parseval's identity:
$$\frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} |P(e^{i\theta})|^2 d\theta = \sum_{k=0}^{n} |a_k|^2 = n+1$$
since each $|a_k|^2 = 1$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `12c068087d665f5ff9c911032dc9e70448320d5ecc508a47a8a53beb8a7f5911`)

```lean
theorem erdos_1150.variants.parseval_lower_bound (P : ℂ[X]) (n : ℕ)
    (hcoeff : ∀ i ≤ P.natDegree, P.coeff i = -1 ∨ P.coeff i = 1)
    (hdeg : P.natDegree = n) :
    ⨆ z : Metric.sphere (0 : ℂ) 1, ‖P.eval (z : ℂ)‖ ≥ Real.sqrt (n + 1)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `dd334510006a46f4b8f82eb42c5d22dae65e971f0e22966f3adda5766589deba`)


#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `ed3c97d825248de52b50483ff36f72138ad685d04e3887e8cde855a362007b0d`)

```text
/--
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ with associated congruence
classes $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ a distinct covering system if every integer satisfies at
least one of these congruences. A minimal distinct covering system is one such
that no proper subset forms a covering system. Let $F(x)$ count the number of
minimal distinct covering systems with all moduli in $[1,x]$. Estimate $F(x)$.

The estimate is `log(log F(x)) / log x → 1`.
-/
```

```lean
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log (coveringCount x : ℝ)) / Real.log (x : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 1)
```

```text
/--
Given any function $f(x)\to \infty$ as $x\to \infty$ there exists a set $A$ with the property
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `d766890b76fac9fb146a60d49bc73f9fac10ea986479f001d70c876a7aee49ed`)

```text
/--
An example of an $A$ with the property that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such that
$a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$ and such that
$$\liminf \frac{\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N^{1/2}}\log N > 0$$
is given by the set of $p^2$, where $p\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is prime.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `5e55268ede10d7d82cabde19f01d0673718a827c7d93f19e1339a0830822970c`)

```lean
theorem erdos_12.variants.example (A : Set ℕ)
    (hA : A = {p ^ 2 | (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (_ : p ≡ 3 [MOD 4])}) :
    IsGood A ∧ 0 < atTop.liminf (fun (N : ℕ) ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard * (N : ℝ).log / √N)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `f4a06edb6680e6e8f27ffa0228732385db51d6334f6112f6595374b4a885c233`)

```lean

    (hA : A = {p ^ 2 | (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (_ : p ≡ 3 [MOD 4])}) :
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `1a0acb5218f95b1167d1ce69a23410367da4c166e953dc1265274110bd06df6a`)

```text
/--
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ be a sequence of integers which tends to infinity sufficiently fast.
If there is an $n$ such that all $n+a_k$ are primes then must there exist infinitely many such $n$?

Erdős [Er80] wrote 'unless I overlook a trivial way of getting a counterexample these questions
are quite hopeless'. There is indeed a trivial counterexample (a variant of the construction in
[erdosproblems.com/429]): define $a_1=2$ and for $k\geq 2$ let $a_k>a_{k-1}$ be a prime such that
$a_k+k\equiv 0\pmod{q_k}$, where $q_k$ is some prime not dividing $k$. This sequence can be made to
grow arbitrarily fast

See also [erdosproblems.com/429] and [erdosproblems.com/1102].
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `8c4495c0e8778d64118287fd321b5ee7ccb899b820d381bf1e242ee470a11f6f`)

```lean
theorem erdos_1209.parts.i :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → (∀ k, f k ≤ a k) →
        (∃ n, ∀ k, (n + a k).Prime) →
        {n | ∀ k, (n + a k).Prime}.Infinite
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `57db36fbbe38983e6d2709e24367112faf023bf0cd1ff26e965c106d222a561a`)

```lean
:
    answer(False) ↔
      ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → (∀ k, f k ≤ a k) →
        (∃ n, ∀ k, (n + a k).Prime) →
        {n | ∀ k, (n + a k).Prime}.Infinite
```

```text
/--
Erdős and Turán proved [ErTu34] in their first joint paper that
$$
  \log n \ll f(n) \ll \frac{n}{\log n}
$$

-/
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `a2de71dba9f9e6bc2dd566ccdf21c0edfd02bf0deff5f3b861a054ad4ec490db`)

```text
/--
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be an infinite set which contains no three points on a
line and no four points on a circle. Consider the graph with vertices the points
in $A$, where two vertices are joined by an edge if and only if they are an
integer distance apart. How large can the chromatic number and clique number of
this graph be? In particular, can the chromatic number be infinite?

The chromatic number can be infinite: there is an infinite general-position set
whose integer-distance graph admits no finite proper colouring. How large the
*clique* number can be is not addressed here.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `35a1c324e129753d05eed945896705d777971f9a23947a0c476cbe8875eb2117`)

```lean
theorem erdos_130 :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∃ A : Set ℝ², A.Infinite ∧ InGeneralPosition A ∧
        (IntegerDistancePlaneGraph A).chromaticNumber = ⊤
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `d97d0436ec327ce584d1c64b454c7f767df626e1422be47d782f8224479dc78f`)

```lean
:
    answer(True) ↔
      ∃ A : Set ℝ², A.Infinite ∧ InGeneralPosition A ∧
        (IntegerDistancePlaneGraph A).chromaticNumber = ⊤
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `bc54e73fa736db09ec0f74dfa21e875126e15a22cdae58a277ce9316fc77ea19`)

```text
/--
Let $\epsilon,\delta>0$ and $n$ be sufficiently large in terms of $\epsilon$ and $\delta$.
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $<n^{1/2-\epsilon}$.
Can $G$ be made into a triangle-free graph with diameter $2$ by adding at most $\delta n^2$ edges?

Asked by Erdős and Gyárfás, who proved that this is the case when $G$ has maximum degree $\ll \log n/\log\log n$. A construction of Simonovits shows that this conjecture is false if we just have maximum degree $\leq Cn^{1/2}$, for some large enough $C$. In this note Alon solves this problem in a strong form, in particular proving that a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $<n^{1/2-\epsilon}$ can be made into a triangle-free graph with diameter $2$ by adding at most $O(n^{2-\epsilon})$ edges.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `278d1d1754dd6df35019520e426a512ac1b4f165693c70e0dc4a2b6b46b31d1c`)

```lean
theorem erdos_134 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ),
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.CliqueFree 3 →
      (∀ v : Fin n, (G.degree v : ℝ) < Real.rpow (n : ℝ) ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε)) →
      ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
        G ≤ H ∧
        H.CliqueFree 3 ∧
        (∀ x y : Fin n, x ≠ y → H.Adj x y ∨ ∃ z, H.Adj x z ∧ H.Adj z y) ∧
        ((H.edgeFinset \ G.edgeFinset).card : ℝ) ≤ δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `d88090e34a2a338673bf7becb4810df62d7559ae16387c1f6de8644b268926a5`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ),
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.CliqueFree 3 →
      (∀ v : Fin n, (G.degree v : ℝ) < Real.rpow (n : ℝ) ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε)) →
      ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
        G ≤ H ∧
        H.CliqueFree 3 ∧

```

```text
/--
The counterexample: a connected bipartite `2`-degenerate `H` whose extremal number exceeds
$n^{3/2+\epsilon}$ infinitely often, so the `r = 2` case of `erdos_146` fails.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `00f2ba210c307328a697f3c0c2009e7a29e04c6c994bca29d6f5a45611f134e1`)

```lean
theorem erdos_146.variants.two_degenerate_counterexample :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)),
      H.Connected ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ IsDegenerate 2 H ∧
      ∃ c ε : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < ε ∧
        ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2 + ε) ≤ (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `2113af12371a7be6c7edfa5010ce468a6909a91f334fa775784d02f3e911bfb6`)

```text
/--
Let $A\subset \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a Sidon set with $\lvert A\rvert\sim N^{1/2}$. Must $A+A$ be
well-distributed over all small moduli? In particular, must about half the elements of $A+A$ be
even and half odd?

The answer is yes. Lindström [Li98] proved the analogous statement for $A$ itself (see
`erdos_154.variants.lindstrom`), later strengthened by Kolountzakis [Ko99]; well-distribution of
$A+A$ then follows using the Sidon property.

We state the question for the sumset: for any sequence of Sidon sets
$A_k\subseteq\{0,\ldots,N_k\}$ with $N_k\to\infty$ and $\lvert A_k\rvert\sim N_k^{1/2}$, and any
modulus $m\geq 2$, the proportion of elements of $A_k+A_k$ congruent to $i\pmod m$ (i.e. the count
divided by $\lvert A_k+A_k\rvert$) tends to $1/m$ for every residue $i<m$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `80d756a10cff2dad0c0be9dd785160d25e352b14072c4eea1b953301d97a5584`)

```lean
theorem erdos_154 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (N : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → Finset ℕ),
      Tendsto (fun k => (N k : ℝ)) atTop atTop →
      (∀ k, ∀ x ∈ A k, x ≤ N k) →
      (∀ k, IsSidon (A k : Set ℕ)) →
      Tendsto (fun k => ((A k).card : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (N k)) atTop (nhds 1) →
      ∀ i < m, Tendsto
        (fun k => (((A k + A k).filter (fun s => s % m = i)).card : ℝ) / ((A k + A k).card : ℝ))
        atTop (nhds (1 / m))
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `7a742836dd8725d7a61e13b1b4a1ec94b01aa8694cb1730920e8dfa381d81b52`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (N : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → Finset ℕ),
      Tendsto (fun k => (N k : ℝ)) atTop atTop →
      (∀ k, ∀ x ∈ A k, x ≤ N k) →
      (∀ k, IsSidon (A k : Set ℕ)) →
      Tendsto (fun k => ((A k).card : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (N k)) atTop (nhds 1) →
      ∀ i < m, Tendsto
        (fun k => (((A k + A k).filter (fun s => s % m = i)).card : ℝ) / ((A k + A k).card : ℝ))
        atTop (nhds (1 / m))
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `f1fb418075cd5cd94c67cd42ee8ec53fbcafeb3eeefcfd25541d0c4b178138b7`)

```text
/--
Is the set of odd integers not of the form $2^k+p$ the union of an infinite arithmetic progression
and a set of density $0$?

Erdős called this conjecture "rather silly".

Chen [Ch23] has proved the answer is no.

This was formalized in Lean by Chin using Aristotle.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `f708fdb735f321926281bec34bd2df24b55e308d1b2d42dbf89b2b9f49ca024b`)

```lean
theorem erdos_16 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∃ A B : Set ℕ, Erdos16Set = A ∪ B ∧
        (∃ a d : ℕ, d > 0 ∧ A = { x | ∃ m : ℕ, x = a + m * d }) ∧
        density_zero B
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `2b720f001ccaf3ba4d6584163b92d9a26aac2aa45f613405c956004bf0aea9a9`)

```lean
        (∃ a d : ℕ, d > 0 ∧ A = { x | ∃ m : ℕ, x = a + m * d }) ∧

```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `e5e54a6b70638fcdefd58ed632a514e501e6572b7e0ff2b78402535c1432b8a2`)

```text
/--
A set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ is primitive if no member of $A$ divides another. Is the sum
$$\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n\log n}$$
maximised over all primitive sets when $A$ is the set of primes?

Erdős [Er35] proved that this sum always converges for a primitive set. Lichtman [Li23] proved
that the answer is yes. An alternative, simpler, proof is given by Alexeev, Barreto, Li, Lichtman,
Price, Shah, Tang, and Tao [ABLLPSTT26].
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `191e03b63f796095768dcbd410a8651f217d74abea58b1f20f1a9e351b369961`)

```lean
theorem erdos_164 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, (∀ a ∈ A, 2 ≤ a) → Erdos1196.IsPrimitive A →
      (∑' a : A, 1 / ((a : ℕ) * Real.log (a : ℕ))) ≤
        ∑' p : {p : ℕ | p.Prime}, 1 / ((p : ℕ) * Real.log (p : ℕ))
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `c0b7363afa427b4cc3624362b537fa927920adacc0e7f4fec3a9abcb8a02653a`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, (∀ a ∈ A, 2 ≤ a) → Erdos1196.IsPrimitive A →
      (∑' a : A, 1 / ((a : ℕ) * Real.log (a : ℕ))) ≤
        ∑' p : {p : ℕ | p.Prime}, 1 / ((p : ℕ) * Real.log (p : ℕ))
```

```text
/--
In 2003, Elsholtz [El03] refined the upper bound to
$$\pi^{\mathcal{C}}(x) \ll x\,\exp\!\bigl(-c(\log\log x)^2\bigr)$$
for every real $0 < c < 1/8$.

[El03] Elsholtz, Christian, On cluster primes. Acta Arith. (2003), 281--284.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `956437bbf89930f35f5874007b6744ed66fe3ed1c6d11e2f51b16fe35430cf4d`)

```lean
theorem erdos_17.variants.upper_Elsholtz :
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (1 / 8),
      IsBigOWith C atTop (fun x ↦ (clusterPrimeCount x : ℝ))
        (fun x ↦ x * exp (-c * (log (log x)) ^ 2))
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `136aa21d34bcf343e763796230c224c3dc99b79eb41c005edd504b55a75d485b`)

```text
Let $R(3;k)$ be the minimal $n$ such that if the edges of $K_n$ are coloured with $k$ colours
then there must exist a monochromatic triangle. Determine

along with the explicit superexponential lower bound in
```

```text
/--
Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS14] proved that $O_\epsilon(n)$ cycles and edges suffice if $G$ has
minimum degree at least $\epsilon n$, for any $\epsilon>0$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `a50e19f7be0d0460c4b6c04661b049d82e3c4a4e01faaccd500dd8be96661b8d`)

```lean
theorem erdos_184.variants.conlon_fox_sudakov :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≥ ε * (Fintype.card V : ℝ) →
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V)
```

```text
/--
If $\mathbb{R}^2$ is finitely coloured then must there exist some colour class which contains the
vertices of a rectangle of every area?

Graham, "On Partitions of 𝔼ⁿ", Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 28, 89-91 (1980).
(See "Concluding Remarks" on page 96.)

Solved (with answer `False`, as formalised below) in:
Vjekoslav Kovač, "Coloring and density theorems for configurations of a given volume", 2023
https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09973
In fact, Kovač's colouring is even Jordan measurable (the topological boundary of each
monochromatic region is Lebesgue measurable and has measure zero).

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev and Kovac using Aristotle.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `6a6ff566aedc0daf6fce6175e0f744bd6dff123dcdf6ac5e4dc33cf700e59b72`)

```lean
theorem erdos_189 :
    answer(False) ↔ Erdos189For
      (fun a b c d ↦
        line[ℝ, a, b].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, b, c].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, b, c].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, c, d].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, c, d].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, d, a].direction)
      (fun a b c d ↦ dist a b * dist b c)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `3533227333378e2134224e1c0ee90ff9cbe573718ed39d37bf28454d58061924`)

```text
/--
The answer is no; Erdős and Graham report this was proved by Baumgartner, presumably referring to
the paper [Ba75], which does not state this exactly, but the following simple construction is
implicit in [Ba75].

Let $P_1,P_2,\ldots$ be an enumeration of all countably many infinite arithmetic progressions. We
choose $a_1$ to be the minimal element of $P_1\cap \mathbb{N}$, and in general choose $a_n$ to be an
element of $P_n\cap \mathbb{N}$ such that $a_n>2a_{n-1}$. By construction $A=\{a_1 < a_2 < \cdots\}$
contains at least one element from every infinite arithmetic progression, and is a lacunary set, so
is certainly Sidon.

AlphaProof has found the following explicit construction: $A = \{ (n+1)!+n : n\geq 0\}$. This is a
Sidon set, and intersects every arithmetic progression, since for any $a,d\in \mathbb{N}$,
$(a+d+1)!+(a+d)\in A$, and $d$ divides $(a+d+1)!+d$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `4b3130ff0e3ec0ed30f9c042b279e192b085047a40bbf1c2062a498ec307bbeb`)

```lean
theorem erdos_198 : (∀ A : Set ℕ, IsSidon A → (∃ Y, IsAPOfLength Y ⊤ ∧ Y ⊆ Aᶜ)) ↔
    answer(False)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `48b69264063bbfaef7118eff9763a7bfad3567a64cedd5569186459c90762ca5`)

```lean
: (∀ A : Set ℕ, IsSidon A → (∃ Y, IsAPOfLength Y ⊤ ∧ Y ⊆ Aᶜ)) ↔
    answer(False)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `59119cdf16bcdab74ce3f3f9f95583a348567d6ea268ff49f39c2ced09369695`)

```text
/--
Are there $n$ such that there is a covering system with moduli the divisors of $n$ which is 'as
disjoint as possible'?

That is, for all $d\mid n$ with $d>1$ there is an associated $a_d$ such that every integer is
congruent to some $a_d\pmod{d}$, and if there is some integer $x$ with
$$x\equiv a_d\pmod{d}\textrm{ and }x\equiv a_{d'}\pmod{d'}$$then $(d,d')=1$.

The density of such $n$ is zero. Erdős and Graham believed that no such $n$ exist.

Adenwalla [Ad25] has proved there are no such $n$.

This was formalized by van Doorn in Lean using Aristotle.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `899c767c3d77069d6cb1c89f1d8ff6081a6f40f05efa8acefa6d157db396bf1d`)

```lean
theorem erdos_204 : answer(False) ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℤ),
    let D := {d : ℕ | d ∣ n ∧ d > 1}
    (∀ x : ℤ, ∃ d ∈ D, x ≡ a d [ZMOD d]) ∧
    (∀ d ∈ D, ∀ d' ∈ D, d ≠ d' → (∃ x : ℤ, x ≡ a d [ZMOD d] ∧ x ≡ a d' [ZMOD d']) →
      Nat.gcd d d' = 1)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `35e5345763be55c4254a83a580d07922fbb12c31bed71c4022a261c70fb482d1`)

```lean
: answer(False) ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℤ),
    let D := {d : ℕ | d ∣ n ∧ d > 1}
    (∀ x : ℤ, ∃ d ∈ D, x ≡ a d [ZMOD d]) ∧
    (∀ d ∈ D, ∀ d' ∈ D, d ≠ d' → (∃ x : ℤ, x ≡ a d [ZMOD d] ∧ x ≡ a d' [ZMOD d']) →
      Nat.gcd d d' = 1)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `ed7514a3cdc8d438a9ef10d6eef953dc3b402b99abf78e9c06dfad0c71ae0c0c`)

```text
/--
Is it true that all sufficiently large $n$ can be written as $2^k+m$ for some $k\geq 0$, where
$\Omega(m)<\log\log m$? (Here $\Omega(m)$ is the number of prime divisors of $m$ counted with
multiplicity.) What about $<\epsilon \log\log m$?

Barreto and Leeham, using ChatGPT and Aristotle, have proved a negative answer, which was
quantified by Tao and Alexeev (see the comments).
-/
```

```lean
theorem erdos_205.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      IsRepresentable (fun m => ε * Real.log (Real.log m)) n
```

```text
/--
In fact there are infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k$ with $2^k<n$, $n-2^k$ has at least
$$\gg \left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}$$
many prime factors.
-/
```

```lean
theorem erdos_205.variants.many_prime_factors : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    {n : ℕ | ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ^ k < n →
      c * Real.sqrt (Real.log n / Real.log (Real.log n)) ≤ (Ω (n - 2 ^ k) : ℝ)}.Infinite
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `47f6362cb396bbad8cf0d00c6937b3418b3e429bfc987d73030e35299fc7931d`)

```text
/--
Let $x>0$ be a real number. For any $n\geq 1$ let
$$R_n(x) = \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{1}{m_i}<x$$
be the maximal sum of $n$ distinct unit fractions which is $<x$.

Is it true that, for almost all $x$, for sufficiently large $n$, we have
$$R_{n+1}(x)=R_n(x)+\frac{1}{m},$$
where $m$ is minimal such that $m$ does not appear in $R_n(x)$ and the right-hand side is
$<x$? (That is, are the best underapproximations eventually always constructed in a 'greedy'
fashion?)

Kovač [Ko24b] has proved that this is false - in fact as false as possible: the set of
$x\in (0,\infty)$ for which the best underapproximations are eventually 'greedy' has Lebesgue
measure zero.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `de4e9244415527df240695680ab6d8db87cdc00eb3b3a8eb733ecd13d4a65db5`)

```lean
theorem erdos_206 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume.restrict (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))), EventuallyGreedy x
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `7e15a0a4240aac3b3501f2da1ed447bde0bf9f9293c9a01d4546bb1cae73fa7f`)

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `96938a63fb41a2ae8605c5155cd1e22cf979d216332d072b230751683d692b8a`)

```text
/--
The construction of Bollobás and Erdős [BoEr76]: for every $\epsilon > 0$ and $\delta > 0$,
for all sufficiently large $n$ there is a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with independence
number at most $\delta n$ and at least $(1/8 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges. Together with
`erdos_22.variants.szemeredi_upper` this shows that the Ramsey–Turán density of $K_4$ is $1/8$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `4df88f2a2ef1942e16816ddee7499962e99e8ecbfb5eb7c6e090e155eaf5b19b`)

```lean
theorem erdos_22.variants.bollobas_erdos_lower (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ δ * n ∧ (1 / 8 - ε) * n ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `b888d487eb0771bb12bfe3206f0f66de51ba47fccf8970817a1181bcc6fb92e1`)

```lean
(ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ δ * n ∧ (1 / 8 - ε) * n ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `fcfa823cf3df06e2daac276e9a386a82bbd56c6607c4a903f4f6aba4f1ae73ff`)

```text
/--
The quantitative strengthening proved by Fox, Loh, and Zhao [FLZ15]: there is a constant
$C > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$ there exists a $K_4$-free graph on $n$
vertices with at least $n^2/8$ edges whose largest independent set has size at most
$$C \cdot \frac{(\log\log n)^{3/2}}{(\log n)^{1/2}} \cdot n.$$
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `52c78fb7f74285e2cd4335792255aee35adc86b73bac4381afb69065fbdb9580`)

```lean
theorem erdos_22.variants.fox_loh_zhao :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤
          C * (Real.log (Real.log n)) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / (Real.log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * n ∧
        (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `0b2a6920fa3b4d2b9ed730da741ee1fc8131f6db80cebf7b0e29a8c223a68930`)

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `3318da170b749d8d925fb5512f38ca5bdcf6c326bc8456c574be3b29ce4e3245`)

```text
/--
Does there exist, for all large $n$, a polynomial $P$ of degree $n$, with coefficients $\pm1$, such
that $$\sqrt n \ll |P(z)| \ll \sqrt n$$ for all $|z|=1$, with the implied constants independent of
$z$ and $n$?

The answer is yes, proved by Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST19].

[BBMST19] Balister, P. and Bollob\'{A}s, B. and Morris, R. and Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., _Flat Littlewood Polynomials Exist_. arXiv:1907.09464 (2019).
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `ad60039415c62161a5c299f2d96f1a865e9ae4f0d5dad35894d489627291bf87`)

```lean
theorem erdos_228 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ (c₁ : ℝ) (c₂ : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.degree = n ∧
    (∀ i ≤ n, p.coeff i = 1 ∨ p.coeff i = -1) ∧
    ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ = 1 →
    ( √n < c₁ * ‖p.eval z‖ ∧ ‖p.eval z‖ < c₂ * √n )
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `bde0412069fde0b5caaaa211ad7c5ad509e89f4e81cb97641ca3375fc50eb36c`)

```text
/--
Every triangle-free graph on $25$ vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most $25$
edges.

This is the $n = 5$ case of Erdős Problem 23.  It follows from the high-density range of
Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky together with McKay's complete catalogue of the 23-vertex extremal
graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `2ca63d7bf0c23ebdcd56dce83fcb8e6cdf3cb8df0f25ceaf2b7ad025b0ee73bb`)

```lean
theorem erdos_23.variants.n5 :
    ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)),
        H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 25
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `cffbd5bbba68834500b24d40b322238a301d577c76d81b2ada4b5ce72b7c9ea0`)

```text
/--
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to \{-1,1\}$ be a multiplicative function. Is it true that
$$ \lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\leq N}f(n)$$ always exists?

The answer is yes, as proved by Wirsing [Wi67], and generalised by Halász [Ha68].
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `979f81cd5742af56e0bb8d21ce43967795f960f81ef88f8a31a82e2cf7dfa841`)

```lean
theorem erdos_239 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ,
    (∀ n ≥ 1, f n = 1 ∨ f n = -1) ∧
    (∀ m n, m.Coprime n → f (m * n) = f m * f n) ∧
    f 1 = 1 →
    ∃ L, Tendsto (fun N ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) / N) atTop (𝓝 L)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `2d9b7b6ec20d546974c93ba77a651fe1e03f834cacaad4a812a44ade4534577f`)

```lean
:
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ,
    (∀ n ≥ 1, f n = 1 ∨ f n = -1) ∧
    (∀ m n, m.Coprime n → f (m * n) = f m * f n) ∧
    f 1 = 1 →
    ∃ L, Tendsto (fun N ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) / N) atTop (𝓝 L)
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `a5f28207a25d0b433e81b1e51af89e9183993ff0dad9a9aabcfafccdb69ed1eb`)

```text
/--
Does every triangle-free graph on $5n$ vertices contain at most $n^5$ copies of $C_5$?

Győri proved this with $1.03n^5$, which has been improved by Füredi. The answer is yes, as proved
independently by Grzesik [Gr12] and Hatami, Hladky, Král, Norine, and Razborov [HHKNR13].
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `b9806a803013eb8afd050e45bf1c8eb65ba81d33c84fe62be760686818078103`)

```lean
theorem erdos_24 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (5 * n))), G.CliqueFree 3 →
      G.copyCount (cycleGraph 5) ≤ n ^ 5
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `8e39470a0361059d541a1c17ea6bebab3502b0b1edc78c7215077fd3e3e1cc58`)

```lean

    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (5 * n))), G.CliqueFree 3 →
      G.copyCount (cycleGraph 5) ≤ n ^ 5
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `fe05e654ed44c58a45391792c7254d1c115eecddd32878150ac8c8e3ea07ca29`)

```text
/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $\lvert A\cap [1,2x]\rvert -\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert \to
\infty\textrm{ as }x\to \infty$ and $\sum_{n\in A} \{ \theta n\}=\infty$ for every $\theta\in
(0,1)$, where $\{x\}$ is the distance of $x$ from the nearest integer. Then every sufficiently large
integer is the sum of distinct elements of $A$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `46fae9d9f79fec31cb96333e2a51568ca00b253f429999e1161f682c0ce7fc5a`)

```lean
theorem erdos_254 :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
      (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 (2 * x)).ncard - (A ∩ Icc 1 x).ncard) atTop atTop) ∧
      (∀ θ : ℝ, 0 < θ → θ < 1 → ¬ Summable (fun n : A ↦ distToNearestInt (θ * (n : ℝ)))) →
        ∀ᶠ m in atTop, IsSumOfDistinct A m
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `5d4aa37a868d02134f67c3dac67c7e95ef147fbb48b33292de416c9979066b8a`)

```lean
:
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
      (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 (2 * x)).ncard - (A ∩ Icc 1 x).ncard) atTop atTop) ∧
      (∀ θ : ℝ, 0 < θ → θ < 1 → ¬ Summable (fun n : A ↦ distToNearestInt (θ * (n : ℝ)))) →
        ∀ᶠ m in atTop, IsSumOfDistinct A m
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `4f27e251e918ecb735d989718cda1d7f003e7320fb6b0c7c5229f35812fac9a2`)

```text
/--
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be infinite such that $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a} = \infty$. Must
there exist some $k\geq 1$ such that almost all integers have a divisor of the form $a+k$
for some $a\in A$?

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `944cd086d2c4a1689c9c28d0cdde5fa33289e5c0400b6eb4be695643f4fe845b`)

```lean
theorem erdos_26 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ A : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono A → IsThick A →
```

```text
/--
A folklore result states that any $a_n$ satisfying $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n^{\frac{1}{2^n}} = \infty$
has $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converging to an irrational number.
-/
```

```lean
    Irrational <| ∑' n, (1 : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ)
```

```text
/--
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] proved that any strictly increasing sequence $a_n$ such that
$\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and $\lim \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n^2} = 0$ is not
an irrationality sequence in the above sense.
```

```lean
    ¬ IsIrrationalitySequence a
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `6beddd790081e6430bf8588da8c2260044efe0ee367a5471eb5509d2497eb8db`)

```text
/--
In fact, Kovač and Tao proved in [KoTa24] that there exists a strictly increasing
sequence $a_n$ of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ converges to a rational
number for all $t \in \mathbb{Q}$ such that $t \ne -a_n$ for any $n$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).
-/
```

```lean
theorem erdos_266.variants.all_rationals:
    ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ a 0 ≥ 1 ∧
      (∀ t : ℚ, (¬ ∃ n : ℕ, t = -(a n)) →
        (∃ q : ℚ, HasSum (fun n : ℕ => ((1 : ℝ) / ((a n) + t))) q))
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `f96d78dc1abdfe555af0b8bd9b018c347f9c06d06545f0439767f953f1abb96b`)

```text
/--
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge c > 1$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `e3628d3c2a3d344a11966cc077709b9bf2926a27c776c7e90c23762e70eebc35`)

```lean
theorem erdos_267 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n : ℕ → ℕ) (c > (1 : ℚ)), StrictMono n → (∀ k, c ≤ n (k+1) / n k) →
    Irrational (∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib <| n k))
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `d5160a9df58c935ef76eaa542f6b3e3d6b55afab828165990c57b48f08c79917`)

```text
/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 3$?

```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `d41b93fc553089e0b0f4c16a0c1ac9f0653404a45e56631f7a465d75d2f4724d`)

```text
/--
If a finite system of $r$ congruences $\{ a_i\pmod{n_i} : 1\leq i\leq r\}$ (the $n_i$ are not
necessarily distinct) covers $2^r$ consecutive integers then it covers all integers.

This is best possible as the system $2^{i-1}\pmod{2^i}$ shows. This was proved independently by
Selfridge and Crittenden and Vanden Eynden [CrVE70].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `6247d8d47ef9aa522609413383267f7de372ada7f1945c55583a739ee7d4cbbb`)

```lean
theorem erdos_275 (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → ℤ) (n : Fin r → ℕ)
    (H : ∃ k : ℤ, ∀ x ∈ Ico k (k + 2 ^ r), ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD n i]) (x : ℤ) :
    ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD n i]
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `9f46ce3cd7fa584320fc7e4b5c050ca87698d7e784b2d57af0f030002301eb7e`)

```lean
(r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → ℤ) (n : Fin r → ℕ)
    (H : ∃ k : ℤ, ∀ x ∈ Ico k (k + 2 ^ r), ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD n i]) (x : ℤ) :
    ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD n i]
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `82dd6fd3a36268d1b67a8c3debc276e2c27068e29ce45abcd1b7969da41a06a6`)

```text
/--
Is it true that, for every $c$, there exists an $n$ such that $\sigma(n)>cn$ but there is no
covering system whose moduli all divide $n$?

This was answered affirmatively by Haight [Ha79].
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `988bbb75a68a6e07fecd8fc2213026d175a6a761feb5d7c35a33016c08a1153b`)

```lean
theorem erdos_277 :
   answer(True) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, ∃ n : ℕ, (σ 1 n : ℝ) > c * n ∧
      ∀ (m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∃ i, (n : ℤ) ∉ m.moduli i
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `0c6132ab6e5dbf564a236560f653b08841d036d2617ac8c2e6ee874e5999f327`)

```text
/--
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots $ be an infinite sequence of integers with associated $a_k\pmod{n_k}$, such that for some $\epsilon>0$ we have $n_k>(1+\epsilon)k\log k$ for all $k$. Then
$$
\#\{ m<n_k : m\not\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i} \textrm{ for }1\leq i\leq k\}\neq o(k).
$$

Cambie observed that this is false.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `d01afd19974657988f437433a4df5ad716c9d0303f920492d8572a4e8ed72fa8`)

```lean

    ∀ (n a : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 1 ≤ i → a i < n i) →
      (∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧
        ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → (n k : ℝ) > (1 + ε) * (k : ℝ) * Real.log (k : ℝ)) →
      ¬ Tendsto
        (fun k : ℕ => (uncoveredCount n a k : ℝ) / (k : ℝ))
        atTop (nhds 0)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `c32e3c2887b888b9269ac915b406ca716cb92a4473df61ecc2948ec2e3403d4d`)

```text
/--
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence such that, for any choice of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$, the set of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ has
density $0$. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists some $k$ such that, for every
choice of congruence classes $a_i$, the density of integers not satisfying any of the congruences
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ is less than $\epsilon$?

The answer is yes; the linked Lean proof formalizes Somani's argument.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `63c9d04d0e553a0591c3cdb2bfaa7e99d0d3b341b66fa17952279575139abf48`)

```lean
theorem erdos_281 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 0 < n i) →
      (∀ a : ResidueChoice n, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidAll n a) 0) →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
          ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ a : ResidueChoice n,
            ∃ d : ℝ, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidPrefix n a k) d ∧ d < ε
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `3697fa38fe1961c41abd97a706448dc3d302c848c2318508cc90bf3bdf1ef034`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 0 < n i) →
      (∀ a : ResidueChoice n, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidAll n a) 0) →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
          ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ a : ResidueChoice n,
            ∃ d : ℝ, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidPrefix n a k) d ∧ d < ε
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `7fa2d19f57ba1f56e05b7f261057caf5d8bb6cd85547339901abe6782bf128a4`)

```text
/--
Let $p\colon \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ be a polynomial whose leading coefficient is
positive and such that there exists no $d≥2$ with $d ∣ p(n)$ for all $n≥1$. Is it true that,
for all sufficiently large $m$, there exist integers $1≤n_1<\dots < n_k$ such that
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$$
and
$$m=p(n_1)+\cdots+p(n_k)$$?

GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Price) has given a proof that the answer is yes, for the stronger version
with $1$ replaced by any rational $\alpha>0$.

This was formalized in Lean by Ammanamanchi using Opus 4.6 and GPT 5.5 Pro.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `7cfcc130347c35ad823b761c5ad56f0bdb51feecfd039916465d117c66892288`)

```lean
theorem erdos_283 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ p : ℤ[X], Condition p
```

```lean
theorem erdos_287.variants.gap_at_least_two :
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `13f448e6abd6e800c4846aa375aa9649c5a035c00f27983ca8777bffb78d7566`)

```text
/--
Let $a\geq 1$. Must there exist some $b>a$ such that
$$\sum_{a\leq n\leq b}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_1}{s_1}\textrm{ and }
\sum_{a\leq n\leq b+1}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_2}{s_2},$$
with $(r_i,s_i)=1$ and $s_2<s_1$? If so, how does this $b(a)$ grow with $a$?

This was resolved in the affirmative by van Doorn [vD24], who proved $b=b(a)$ always exists, and in
fact $b(a) \ll a$. Indeed, if $a\in (3^k,3^{k+1}]$ then one can take $b=2\cdot 3^{k+1}-1$. van Doorn
also proves that $b(a)>a+(1/2-o(1))\log a$, and considers various generalisations of the original
problem.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `6fc2ba430ea60b3275cb9871b4da5b9f42f076e29f70956680394d858bbbe4c3`)

```lean
theorem erdos_290 : answer(True) ↔
    (∀ a : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → ∃ b : ℕ, a < b ∧ harmonicDen a (b + 1) < harmonicDen a b)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `f5a13f72fe96a775e1123009ec419946db137362aea2e288158a32120ee296eb`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    (∀ a : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → ∃ b : ℕ, a < b ∧ harmonicDen a (b + 1) < harmonicDen a b)
```

```text
/--
Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)>1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

Steinerberger has observed that the answer to the second question is trivially yes: for example, any
$n$ which begins with a $2$ in base $3$ has $3\mid (a_n,L_n)$.
-/
```

```lean
theorem erdos_291.parts.ii :
    answer(True) ↔
      { n : ℕ | Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) > 1 }.Infinite
```

- 来源引用 / Source refs：`SRC-MATH-V5-FORMAL-CONJECTURES-2270D31E`

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `999a5f9e288490f0a91c993dc9d46eb15bd8d15e7c9fc62a7b3923217aec16ce`)

```text
/--
Does every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive density contain some finite $S \subset A$ such that
$\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$?

The answer is yes, proved by Bloom [Bl21] (even if 'positive density' is interpreted as 'positive
upper density', which is likely what Erdős intended).

The theorem below uses the positive-upper-density interpretation; the literal natural-density
interpretation is recorded separately.

This was formalized in Lean 3 by Bloom and Mehta.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `aa0196bbacd1f11ccbdc47dbb3bea7932938e75fb1e43a465f65a30627eb8078`)

```lean
theorem erdos_298 : answer(True) ↔ (∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity →
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ), ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `9757c1f320373c42e4d299466616ed9f3db282f612e19fea637759eaa6c64078`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔ (∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity →
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ), ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `96257af6ac9eb50494f2e92ff1f5d38c4b54ea95e84fcf309d71387ae800eac1`)

```text
/--
Is there an infinite sequence $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$ and no finite
sum of $\frac{1}{a_i}$ is equal to 1?

There does not exist such a sequence, which follows from the positive solution to
[erdosproblems.com/298] by Bloom [Bl21].

This was formalized in Lean 3 by Bloom and Mehta.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `0e3c3775cb5fab2005a281e3892b8feb7ccd3b012d4683362f257d5c1e25eec4`)

```lean
theorem erdos_299 : answer(False) ↔ (∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono a ∧ (∀ n, 0 < a n) ∧
    (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) - a n) =O[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ S : Finset ℕ, ∑ i ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / a i ≠ 1)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `3841b72a1f7e8781bdf602ff6f69550694c1fb8b531edcbc567520ef3797cfa9`)

```lean
: answer(False) ↔ (∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono a ∧ (∀ n, 0 < a n) ∧
    (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) - a n) =O[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ S : Finset ℕ, ∑ i ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / a i ≠ 1)
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `f78599a6f42dd995f05d8af8adcae0c49397ebf5b8cc509a2d1697ec1404409d`)

```text
/--
The corresponding question is also false if one replaces sequences such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$
with sets of positive density, as follows from [Bl21].

The statement is as follows:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has positive upper density (and hence certainly if $A$ has positive
density) then there is a finite $S \subset A$ such that $\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `561ade4a93ce53b0c10ecb76f6fc12798704c8d9e1b63c503106226ee76deebb`)

```lean
theorem erdos_299.variants.density : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity →
    ∃ S : Finset ℕ, ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / n = 1
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `708f35aa3ad5bef78ff707aa3d592f18700d7af468e38897c546310491fd72c7`)


### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `3358dfb5eb5abaf311f7d2368d7a6e4f09d04662bffd82bff78d3d8878d20f7e`)

```text
/--
Is it true that in any finite colouring of the integers there exists a monochromatic solution
to $\frac 1 a = \frac 1 b + \frac 1 c$ with distinct $a, b, c$?

This is true, as proved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].

This was formalized in Lean by Yuan using Seed-Prover.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `9f509aa5fed37a1c6032bb38f97d7cbc7cf03fa35178b4c229e4a97b1a207ccf`)

```lean
theorem erdos_303 :
    answer(True) ↔
    -- For any finite colouring of the integers
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℤ → ℤ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      -- There exists integers `a, b, c`
      ∃ (a b c : ℤ),
      -- that are non-zero and distinct.
      [a, b, c, 0].Nodup ∧
      -- `a, b, c` satisfy the equation
      (1/a : ℝ) = 1/b + 1/c ∧
      -- `a, b, c` have the same color
      (𝓒 '' {a, b, c}).Subsingleton
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `689f1130be952e7fb85c5db51524960bb8d60e26bd77ceec77f17ed3e2ca88ba`)

```lean
:
    answer(True) ↔
    -- For any finite colouring of the integers
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℤ → ℤ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      -- There exists integers `a, b, c`
      ∃ (a b c : ℤ),
      -- that are non-zero and distinct.
      [a, b, c, 0].Nodup ∧
      -- `a, b, c` satisfy the equation
      (1/a : ℝ) = 1/b + 1/c ∧
      -- `a, b, c` have the same color
      (𝓒 '' {a, b, c}).Subsingleton
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `87f88f865de2bbeb04f900afcda46bfc427c2847e784feb74e6893b22d4d03f0`)

```text
/--
Instead of asking for sets of primes, ask only that all elements in the sets be relatively coprime.

Cambie has found several examples when this weakened version is true. For example,
$$
1=\left(1+\frac{1}{5}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right)
$$
and
$$
1=\left(1+\frac{1}{41}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{7}\right).
$$
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `6b7db359487eb0c2a96907694436ebc63598e72f56bf082f34cf9aad4bb29fe7`)

```lean
theorem erdos_307.variants.coprime : answer(True) ↔ ∃ P Q : Finset ℕ, 0 ∉ P ∩ Q ∧ 1 < #P ∧ 1 < #Q ∧
    Set.Pairwise P Nat.Coprime ∧ Set.Pairwise Q Nat.Coprime ∧
    1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (p : ℚ)⁻¹) * (∑ q ∈ Q, (q : ℚ)⁻¹)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `885132bfa61ab5ba46a74b3c3359e6a9e00c71381fecc59e71d2d001ad9dd4c3`)

```lean

    1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (p : ℚ)⁻¹) * (∑ q ∈ Q, (q : ℚ)⁻¹)
```

```text
/--
Given any infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ there is a set $B$ of density $0$ such that $A+B$ contains all except finitely many integers.

Conjectured by Erdős and Straus. Proved by Lorentz [Lo54].
-/
```

```lean
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, B.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `ce6b4845143b90c7b7551e446c984fc70efb3c6941af95c0a5a283fa87498ff8`)

```text
/--
Let $n\geq 1$ and let $m$ be minimal such that $\sum_{n\leq k\leq m}\frac{1}{k}\geq 1$. We define
$$\epsilon(n) = \sum_{n\leq k\leq m}\frac{1}{k}-1.$$
How small can $\epsilon(n)$ be? Is it true that
$$\liminf n^2\epsilon(n)=0?$$

This is true, and shown by Lim and Steinerberger [LiSt24], who further proved that, for any
$\delta>0$, there exist infinitely many $n$ and $m$ such that
$$n^2\left\lvert \sum_{n\leq k\leq m}\frac{1}{k}-1\right\rvert\ll \frac{1}{(\log n)^{5/4-\delta}}.$$
Erdős and Graham (and also Lim and Steinerberger) believe that the exponent of $2$ is best
possible here, in that $\liminf \epsilon(n) n^{2+\delta}=\infty$ for all $\delta>0$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `24cf0e3b52bc732e2e9a8fb612adc7d0cc9e056af58789bd3d8554c082dabf8e`)

```lean
theorem erdos_314 : answer(True) ↔
    atTop.liminf (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * epsilon n) = 0
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `f6ecc94270beb3cf2b3dd027a1e573418b1d16d277e00d74c71f2d0059411fb9`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    atTop.liminf (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * epsilon n) = 0
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `b506c2c870069ef390166e7f1806b60f932dc5fd0df4001af5116bda78b14050`)

```text
/--
This is not true in general, as shown by Sándor [Sa97], who observed that the proper divisors of
$120$ form a counterexample. More generally, Sándor shows that for any $n\geq 2$ there exists a
finite set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}\backslash\{1\}$ with $\sum_{k\in A}\frac{1}{k} < n$ and no
partition into $n$ parts each of which has $\sum_{k\in A_i}\frac{1}{k}<1$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `873ce77ff5b33446943ea894ac6af88df2a87be0fe92c728a40a6101a0b349c1`)

```lean
theorem erdos_316.variants.generalized (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ A : Finset ℕ,
    A.Nonempty ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 ∉ A ∧ ∑ k ∈ A, (1 / k : ℚ) < n ∧ ∀ P : Finpartition A,
    P.parts.card = n → ∃ p ∈ P.parts, 1 ≤ ∑ n ∈ p, (1 / n : ℚ)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `49bd90d30dd3d46fecdc82482237484888acd121d93bedba63ec87ca195f1d13`)

```lean
(n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ A : Finset ℕ,
    A.Nonempty ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 ∉ A ∧ ∑ k ∈ A, (1 / k : ℚ) < n ∧ ∀ P : Finpartition A,
    P.parts.card = n → ∃ p ∈ P.parts, 1 ≤ ∑ n ∈ p, (1 / n : ℚ)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `80ed09c1449aa1fe3b8a10bf7ef87905427124d07de23095c5860d0250e0c094`)

```text
/--
Suppose $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ and $C>0$ is such that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\leq C$ for all
$n\in\mathbb{N}$. Can $A$ be partitioned into $t$ many subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_t$ (where
$t=t(C)$ depends only on $C$) such that $1_{A_i}\ast 1_{A_i}(n)<C$ for all $1\leq i\leq t$
and $n\in \mathbb{N}$?

The answer is no. Asked by Erdős and Newman. Nešetřil and Rödl [NeRo85] have shown the
answer is no for all $C$ (even if $t$ is also allowed to depend on $A$).

Erdős [Er80e] had previously shown the answer is no for $C=3,4$ and infinitely many other
values of $C$.

See also [774].

The linked proof writes the representation function as
`Set.ncard {p : ℕ × ℕ | p.1 ∈ A ∧ p.2 ∈ A ∧ p.1 + p.2 = n}`, which counts the same ordered
pairs as `sumRep`, and states the partition condition as a named definition with the same two
conjuncts used below. Its `∃ t` additionally carries `1 ≤ t`, which costs nothing: `t = 0`
forces `A = ∅`, and `A = {1}` has all representation counts at most `C` for `C ≥ 1`.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `c3261c11b6dc0358fce46c7a763aa872f77f8590a74e58e0ae1bdfc66178a20a`)

```lean
theorem erdos_328 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ C : ℕ, 0 < C →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ A : Set ℕ, (∀ n, sumRep A n ≤ C) →
        ∃ P : Fin t → Set ℕ, (⋃ i, P i) = A ∧
          Set.univ.PairwiseDisjoint P ∧
          ∀ i, ∀ n, sumRep (P i) n < C
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `3ffc23fccde77af21ae3918e6a51486a61e178ad67349fa80b9455fbfe6c671e`)

```lean
: answer(False) ↔
    ∀ C : ℕ, 0 < C →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ A : Set ℕ, (∀ n, sumRep A n ≤ C) →
        ∃ P : Fin t → Set ℕ, (⋃ i, P i) = A ∧
          Set.univ.PairwiseDisjoint P ∧
          ∀ i, ∀ n, sumRep (P i) n < C
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `e4f9af8e7449400173f96cf2efab378db3771dda1e93819b02a4d4c07eab8fad`)

```text
/--
Does there exist a minimal basis $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ with positive density
such that, for any $n \in A$, the (upper) density of integers which
cannot be represented without using $n$ is positive?

Neither set is asked to have a density, only to have positive upper density, so
`Set.upperDensity` is used for both rather than `Set.HasPosDensity`. As with many of Erdős'
questions "positive density" here most likely means positive upper density, and in [Er80] he
considers either the lower or the upper density for the integers not representable without a
fixed `n`. Requiring the density to exist would ask a strictly harder question than the one
posed. See #3979.

Such a set exists, so the answer is yes. The linked proof gives one of order `2`.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `ea1ba668b614eb4dc47f571a22d7301eeba38c8dffa25ca4b401c30a4f8030ea`)

```lean
theorem erdos_330_statement :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ (A : Set ℕ), ∃ h, MinAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder A h ∧
    0 < A.upperDensity ∧ ∀ n ∈ A, 0 < (UnrepWithout A n h).upperDensity
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `99a58b81f2a2d6e23b1f575e0a54ceea806297d3018285c76170b07786d81db0`)

```lean

    0 < A.upperDensity ∧ ∀ n ∈ A, 0 < (UnrepWithout A n h).upperDensity
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `5163033c10f375cc4fb800d2db008b23f071ac64d91747d1b15f341920413771`)

```text
/--
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for all large $N$$$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg
N^{1/2}$$and$$\lvert B\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg N^{1/2}.$$
Is it true that there are infinitely many solutions to $a_1-a_2=b_1-b_2\neq 0$ with $a_1,a_2\in A$
and $b_1,b_2\in B$?

Ruzsa has observed that there is a simple counterexample: take $A$ to be the set of numbers whose
binary representation has only non-zero digits in even places, and $B$ similarly but with non-zero
digits only in odd places. It is easy to see $A$ and $B$ both grow like $\gg N^{1/2}$ and yet for
any $n\geq 1$ there is exactly one solution to $n=a+b$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$.

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `db0973f7016faf830b82a81b73e136919e0e517af805abd9fe8dab712931867d`)

```lean
theorem erdos_331 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∀ A B : Set ℕ,
      (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count A n : ℝ)) →
      (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count B n : ℝ)) →
      { s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | let ⟨a₁, a₂, b₁, b₂⟩ := s
        a₁ ∈ A ∧ a₂ ∈ A ∧ b₁ ∈ B ∧ b₂ ∈ B ∧
        a₁ ≠ a₂ ∧ a₁ + b₂ = a₂ + b₁ }.Infinite
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `8eff0fe7790c5fbf92edbab73f938743e30de646cc226e2f07bd5637ab1a884e`)

```lean
:

      ∀ A B : Set ℕ,
      (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count A n : ℝ)) →
      (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count B n : ℝ)) →
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `60101fc03dbc70d4b8c09abb6dfe2199e39733184ef996dc13ab15e957347641`)

```text
/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an additive basis (of any finite order) such that
$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert=o(N)$. Is it true that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty?
$$

The answer is no, and a counterexample was provided by Turjányi [Tu84]. This was generalised (to
the replacement of $A+A$ by the $h$-fold sumset $hA$ for any $h\geq 2$) by Ruzsa and Turjányi
[RT85].

"Additive basis" is `Set.IsAsymptoticAddBasis`: some finite $h$ has $hA$ containing every
sufficiently large integer. The exact notion `Set.IsAddBasis`, which asks that $hA$ be all of
$\mathbb{N}$, would force $0, 1 \in A$ and is not the class these results are about.

The linked file states the basis hypothesis as `∃ N₀, Set.Ici N₀ ⊆ iterated_sumset A k` and
indexes both counting functions by a real $x$ through $\lfloor x\rfloor$, where the counting
functions here are indexed by $N : \mathbb{N}$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `1e8267b38fc41135d5fc67e5e27c078428158ba271f0f52f546411e127ffb7a0`)

```lean
theorem erdos_337 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis →
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `96575c5fb7d2b2a31b94dbdb0d0142a218205dae02505ad86a8099093fffcdce`)

```text
/--
For any permutation $\pi\in S_n$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $S(\pi)$ count the number of distinct consecutive sums, that is, sums of the shape $\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}\pi(i)$. Is it true that
$$
S(\pi) = o(n^2)
$$
for all $\pi\in S_n$?

Hegyvári [He86] gave a counterexample.
-/
```

```lean
theorem erdos_34 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      ((consecutiveSums n p).card : ℝ) < c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `080cc5aba1f615f8e698159f641ea7dc018b437fed52db0cb203906d1a144efd`)

```text
/-- For $0 < \alpha \le 1$ and any $t > 0$, $(t, \alpha)$ is not a good pair: every term
$\lfloor t\alpha^n\rfloor$ lies in the finite interval $[0, \lfloor t\rfloor]$ (since
$\alpha^n \le 1$), so every subset sum is bounded by the constant $\sum_{i \in [0,\lfloor t\rfloor]} i$,
and no large integer can be a subset sum. A partial result on the open Erdős Problem 349,
complementing the $2 < \alpha$ and integer-coefficient cases. -/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `42dea8f7844a32adee1fb2dbd148c036b2fdda95cc4205ee34ce4f9708430b57`)

```lean
    ¬ IsGoodPair t α
```

```text
/-- **Binary expansion.** Every natural number $k$ is a sum of distinct powers of two: there is
a finite set $E$ of exponents with $k = \sum_{i \in E} 2^i$. Proved by strong induction:
subtract the largest power $2^m \le k$, recurse on the remainder. -/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `16cd4c558c0dc77f2dac6f5723e67540b30080c44c41a6b5569c7f0a8547d6d4`)

```lean
theorem exists_finset_sum_two_pow (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ E : Finset ℕ, k = ∑ i ∈ E, 2 ^ i
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `a99a2ba00fbc167f4971a684798695f3e83884a51f53d85499ba8f26310edc7f`)

```text
/--
For any $k$ there exists some $t_k\in (0,1)$ such that the set of $\alpha$
such that the sequence $\lfloor t_k\alpha^n\rfloor$ is complete consists of at least $k$
disjoint line segments.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `37c5fa0c48867cf19abb9e0956af2c12da6410267eee6d7269889381182d75ee`)

```lean
theorem exists_t_for_k_disjoint_segments (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ t ∈ Ioo 0 1, ∃ (ι : Type), k ≤ (Set.univ : Set ι).encard ∧ ∃ I : ι → Set ℝ,
      (∀ i, 2 ≤ (I i).encard ∧ (I i).Nonempty ∧ IsConnected (I i)) ∧
      Pairwise (Disjoint on I) ∧ (⋃ i, I i) ⊆ {α | α > 0 ∧ IsGoodPair t α}
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `cccc8f010e2bfc7258aef19a527dcd8fd0f9d5cd1530a3dbc357b9fb08be5dd2`)

```text
/-- **Integer leading coefficient $t \ge 2$ blocks completeness.** For every integer base
$\alpha$, the pair $(t, \alpha)$ with integer $t \ge 2$ is not good: $\lfloor t\alpha^n\rfloor =
t\alpha^n$ is a multiple of $t$, so every subset sum is too, but two consecutive large integers
cannot both be multiples of $t$. Generalizes the parity obstruction ($t = 2$). A partial result
on Erdős Problem 349. -/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `dd40303584def7f1518d30b19f2f3cd61e08b8605a683f3b9ef3305fc79c9769`)

```lean
theorem int_coeff_ge_two_not_isGoodPair (t : ℤ) (ht : 2 ≤ t) (α : ℤ) :
    ¬ IsGoodPair (t : ℝ) (α : ℝ)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `b00f665958b09a176d7340830d7c5d68a3275846a29bd661816e58a74603ee8a`)

```lean
(t : ℤ) (ht : 2 ≤ t) (α : ℤ) :
    ¬ IsGoodPair (t : ℝ) (α : ℝ)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `d6f40199cc1b36b44433b097cc4d8efb9464c15310ca8292872149efe81fcc4f`)

```text
/--
If `A ⊂ ℕ` is a finite set of integers all of whose subset sums are distinct then `∑ n ∈ A, 1/n < 2`.
Proved by Ryavec.

This was proved by Ryavec, who did not appear to ever publish the proof. Ryavec's proof is
reproduced in [BeEr74]. More generally, Ryavec's proof delivers that
$\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}\leq 2-2^{1-\lvert A\rvert},$ with equality if and only if
$A=\{1,2,\ldots,2^k\}$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `f82104a3563a1241d82cb736604ab1458d342828cf5a98e05dd5df65a3002db0`)

```lean
theorem erdos_350 (A : Finset ℕ) (hA : DecidableDistinctSubsetSums A) :
    ∑ n ∈ A, (1 / n : ℝ) < 2
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `36fdaefc0c2c024a163685f7a0671e7d09069bdbc6a5d41fe5493bc2a829bad0`)

```lean
(A : Finset ℕ) (hA : DecidableDistinctSubsetSums A) :
    ∑ n ∈ A, (1 / n : ℝ) < 2
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `8b6b4937b1758143678543131f9b23911b35bcf544220593bc3dd023698f6510`)

```text
/--
Let $p(x) \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ be a non-constant rational polynomial with positive leading
coefficient. Is it true that $$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$ is strongly complete,
in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers? -/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `5b679c7fc0d5fee938828020bbc33a55c5b10aa940e38f2633b23d0efc0153fd`)

```lean
theorem erdos_351 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ P : ℚ[X], 0 < P.natDegree → 0 < P.leadingCoeff → HasCompleteImage P
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `b079bee8e7795f41fe0eb54a317eba5f8469f669db894c302061ae45f8d89f45`)

```lean
:
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ P : ℚ[X], 0 < P.natDegree → 0 < P.leadingCoeff → HasCompleteImage P
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `568eb734da4008d6fcea0fb498bca69973d7fef8530eb5ee22fe629a4893161f`)

```text
/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct.
It is known that $f(n) \geq (2+o(1))\sqrt{n}$.
Source: See comment by Desmond Weisenberg here: https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/357.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `212ac4fb25684d05bab5383566aa51adc2ecceff7099a5c8ea56bdf59e07b88a`)

```lean
theorem erdos_357.variants.weisenberg : ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (2 + o n) * √n ≤ f n
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `510ded961a5c0680b4ed320b056cb919b6db9b679a9d64c8d45fa14f3e7adb6d`)

```text
/--
Let $\epsilon>0$ and $k\geq 2$. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there is a
sequence of $k$ consecutive integers in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ all of which are $n^\epsilon$-smooth?

The problem is trivially true as written (simply taking $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ and $n>k^{1/\epsilon}$).
There are (at least) two possible variants which are non-trivial, and it is not clear which
Erdős and Graham meant. We formalize the second: each $m\in P$ (where $P$ is the sequence of $k$
consecutive integers sought for) must be in $[n/2,n]$. In this case a positive answer also
follows directly from the result of Balog and Wooley [BaWo98] for infinitely many $n$. Proving
this is true for all large $n$ does not follow immediately from [BaWo98], but can be deduced
using a similar construction, as shown by SkyYang.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `4208729338e363b0ddc50278d6496ec68105272feb2f477277740a412ac6cc49`)

```lean
theorem erdos_369 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k),
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ a : ℕ, n / 2 ≤ a + 1 ∧ a + k ≤ n ∧
        ∀ j < k, ∀ p ∈ (a + 1 + j).primeFactors, (p : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ ε
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `e0838eb7d9a471a2e51ca2ba32984b46e4666e223f546aa7f24148130745f412`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k),
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ a : ℕ, n / 2 ≤ a + 1 ∧ a + k ≤ n ∧
        ∀ j < k, ∀ p ∈ (a + 1 + j).primeFactors, (p : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ ε
```

```text
/--
Show that if `P(n(n+1)) / log n → ∞` where `P(m)` denotes the largest prime factor of `m`, then
the equation `n!=a_1!a_2!···a_k!`, with `n−1 > a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ ··· ≥ a_k`, has only
finitely many solutions.
-/
```

```lean
    (H : Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) => (n*(n+1)).maxPrimeFac / (n : ℝ).log) Filter.atTop) :
    S.Finite
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `ed94c2afdbea348311eb9893da2a741fc2fddc7e859cd9cf84c27338d5f94a0c`)

```text
/-- There exists a constant `c > 0` such that for all `n`, if
`k < c * (log n / (log (log n))) ^ 3 → (∀ i < k, ¬ (n + i + 1).Prime)`, then
there are distinct primes `p₁, ... pₖ` such that `pᵢ ∣ n + i` for all `1 ≤ i ≤ k`. This is proved
in [RST75]. There is no need to only consider sufficiently large `n` because one can always take
`c` small enough so that `k < c * (log n / (log (log n))) ^ 3` implies that `k = 0` until `n` is
large. -/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `6392282f153866623196b568861e1eeddfc3f9d84d6ecba277e5084e8f7e2915`)

```lean
theorem erdos_375.variants.log : ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ,
    k < c * (Real.log n / (Real.log (Real.log n))) ^ 3 → (∀ i < k, ¬ (n + i + 1).Prime) →
    ∃ p : Fin k → ℕ, p.Injective ∧ ∀ i, (p i).Prime ∧ p i ∣ n + i + 1
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `99f2d0fec72c632570389602d46f851e0856a65382fd38eabcee2d5314ceb620`)

```lean
: ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ,
    k < c * (Real.log n / (Real.log (Real.log n))) ^ 3 → (∀ i < k, ¬ (n + i + 1).Prime) →
    ∃ p : Fin k → ℕ, p.Injective ∧ ∀ i, (p i).Prime ∧ p i ∣ n + i + 1
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `6f61ea4774812373bbfe9ee5e92ee374566323afe134222984f4b633ec97bd18`)

```text
/--
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then for almost all integers $f(m) = \gamma_0 + o(1)$.

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `6a6ae24b9ab81439b6b0531d0b90fe560513580c6e3a3bd37c0e9d338163f9d5`)

```lean
theorem erdos_377.variants.ae (γ₀ : ℝ) (hγ₀ : γ₀ = ∑' (k : ℕ), (k + 2 : ℝ).log / 2 ^ (k + 2)) :
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0)),
      ∀ᶠ n in cofinite, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n = γ₀ + o n
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `1184754591342f51eb79ac38d39a2c254faa71fa2d4c3082cebdc0013b46552e`)

```lean

    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0)),
      ∀ᶠ n in cofinite, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n = γ₀ + o n
```

```text
/--
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `55d12528859c5d4ed5c592fd4a754ec00d442b2e3a90ff7a3262004c9166176b`)

```text
/--
Does there exist $B \subset \mathbb{N}$ which is not an additive basis,
but is such that for every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of Schnirelmann density $\alpha$
and every $N$ there exists $b \in B$ such that
$$
  \lvert (A \cup (A+b)) \cap \{1, \ldots, N\} \rvert \geq (\alpha + f(\alpha)) N
$$
where $f(\alpha) > 0$ for $0 < \alpha < 1$?

Note: here Erdős seems to use a slightly weaker notion of an additive basis (see [Er56] at the top
of page 135). In particular, for this problem, a set is an additive basis of order $k$ if every
natural number can be written as a sum of _at most_ $k$ elements of the set, rather than as a sum of
_precisely_ $k$ elements.

A positive [solution](https://github.com/spicylemonade/erdos-38) was given by GPT 5.5 Pro
(prompted by gebyjaff, cleanup by Liam Price); in fact a sparse random set $B$ has this property,
with $f(\alpha)\gg \alpha (1-\alpha)^2$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `d1844bd6d8b435402548b5143f6d6da742411c8b8d0913f9ca744d57b28db74e`)

```lean
theorem erdos_38 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, ¬ B.IsWeakAddBasis ∧ ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ α, 0 < α → α < 1 → f α > 0) ∧
      ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ),
        let α := schnirelmannDensity A
        ∃ b ∈ B, (Ioc 0 N ∩ (A ∪ (A + {b}))).ncard ≥ (α + f α) * N
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `2be6eb426c3d843221adaebef764da0cc12d956af7649aeb7787fac36f3025fd`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, ¬ B.IsWeakAddBasis ∧ ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ α, 0 < α → α < 1 → f α > 0) ∧
      ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ),
        let α := schnirelmannDensity A
        ∃ b ∈ B, (Ioc 0 N ∩ (A ∪ (A + {b}))).ncard ≥ (α + f α) * N
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `919ad68fbdc5872cc3b0a077a5531d8116c2b2d2d8271fc66a11a8b5c46e9797`)

```text
/--
Erdős and Obláth observed that the Bertrand-style fact (first proved by Breusch [Br32]) that, if
$q_i$ is the sequence of primes congruent to $3\pmod{4}$ then $q_{i+1}<2q_i$ except for $q_1=3$,
together with Fermat's theorem on the sums of two squares implies that the only solution to
$n!=x^2+y^2$ is $6!=12^2+24^2$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `2d160204e98dd8f9206663a8b12fbc1bad87ebe0191ce8bc09c7820efdd27621`)

```lean
theorem erdos_399.variants.sum_two_squares :
    ∀ {n x y : ℕ}, 1 < x * y → n ! = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 →
      n = 6 ∧ (x = 12 ∧ y = 24 ∨ x = 24 ∧ y = 12)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `5294948839707edeaec7737732d81d8924491df67a63d8eaf585df3592459d3f`)

```lean
:
    ∀ {n x y : ℕ}, 1 < x * y → n ! = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 →
      n = 6 ∧ (x = 12 ∧ y = 24 ∨ x = 24 ∧ y = 12)
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `8042eb26d179f4304088f7b0efe9818c95c98b187dfe6de6819e1a156cc807da`)

```text
/--
Is there some function $f(r)$ such that $f(r)\to \infty$ as $r\to\infty$, such that, for
infinitely many $n$, there exist $a_1,a_2$ with
$$a_1+a_2> n+f(r)\log n$$
such that $a_1!a_2! \mid n!2^n3^n\cdots p_r^n$?

It is ambiguous in [ErGr80] what the intended quantifiers are on the variables (they write 'is
it true that we can find $a_1+a_2>n+f(r)\log n$...'). Comparing to previous problems such as
[728] and [729] it seems most likely that they intended to ask the formulation in the problem
statement.

The answer is yes: Barreto and Leeham have used ChatGPT to provide a proof of the stated problem
(in fact essentially the same construction as their solution to [729]).
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `b7e7152c0eed481303ebb184e9e6c5a7ed2cbb340a6850cb8e8b20f96d93e3de`)

```lean
theorem erdos_401 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r),
        {n : ℕ | ∃ a₁ a₂ : ℕ, 0 < a₁ ∧ 0 < a₂ ∧
          (a₁ : ℝ) + a₂ > n + f r * Real.log n ∧
          a₁.factorial * a₂.factorial ∣
            n.factorial * (∏ i ∈ Finset.range r, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i) ^ n}.Infinite
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `dedbd4f7a59b578ab5722451defe03d49dd53e366eb5e50cc762af196fed5621`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r),
        {n : ℕ | ∃ a₁ a₂ : ℕ, 0 < a₁ ∧ 0 < a₂ ∧
          (a₁ : ℝ) + a₂ > n + f r * Real.log n ∧
          a₁.factorial * a₂.factorial ∣
            n.factorial * (∏ i ∈ Finset.range r, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i) ^ n}.Infinite
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `92d35b95d6317bda57913c596ee61deacc8ea235dea3ff2d1398822dfc2cb3ad`)

```text
/-- A conjecture of Graham [Gr70], who also conjectured that (assuming $A$ itself
has no common divisor) the only cases where equality is achieved are when
$A = \{1, \dots, n\}$ or $A = \{L/1, \dots, L/n\}$ (where $L = \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, n)$) or
$A = \{2, 3, 4, 6\}$.
Note: The source [BaSo96] mentioned on the Erdős page makes it clear what
quantifiers to use for "where equality is achieved". See Theorem 1.1 there.

TODO(firsching): Consider if we should have the other direction here as well or
an iff statement.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `1004ab3735a1a7f231d2b934b7c0a61f23e7d29f817a86a49fdbedf61b3699d0`)

```lean
theorem erdos_402.variants.equality (A : Finset ℕ) (h₁ : 0 ∉ A) (h₂ : A.Nonempty)
    (h₃ : A.gcd id = 1)
    (h : ∀ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A), (a / A.card : ℚ) ≤ a.gcd b) :
    A = Finset.Icc 1 A.card ∨
    A = (Finset.Icc 1 A.card).image ((Finset.Icc 1 A.card).lcm id / ·) ∨
    A = {2, 3, 4, 6}
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `ccbeae405882cab359110551ed5867b6a396b4f54bb890cecb99d35ece18d68f`)

```text
/--
It follows from a slight strengthening of the Goldbach conjecture that every odd number can be
written as $n - \phi(n)$.
In particular, we assume that every even number greater than 6 can be written as the sum of two
*distinct* primes, in contrast to the usual Goldbach conjecture that every even number greater than
2 can be written as the sum of two primes.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `900d258673a58d1716537190cddd7abf98d35fa1997b9cddac464f70b882a693`)

```lean
theorem erdos_418.variants.conditional
    (goldbach : ∀ (n : ℕ), 6 < n → Even n → ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ n = p + q)
    (m : ℕ) (h : Odd m) :
    ∃ n, m + n.totient = n
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `077bfe6b3e2b9db1d2806e09773ce5eb44466ed89f11aab5f3e8512e9b231a9d`)

```lean
    (m : ℕ) (h : Odd m) :
    ∃ n, m + n.totient = n
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `08ffeb1bc29b1f88619f02f6db6c7fb65b2539a5e14b67751d292e1eec3deef9`)

```text
/--
Erdős [Er73b] has shown that a positive density set of natural numbers cannot be written as
$\sigma(n)-n$ (numbers not of this form are called nonaliquot, or sometimes untouchable).

The density sits in an existential, so `HasPosDensity` is the *stronger* reading: the witness
`S` is ours to choose, and weakening it to positive lower density would claim less rather than
more. That is the opposite of the usual situation for Erdős' "positive density", where the
density is a hypothesis or a claim about a fixed set. Whether the nonaliquot numbers themselves
have a density is a separate question and is not what this states.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `c288562b9c692d3fac3e18e74e05b483273a18b862f6f51b8d934ef14ff7f380`)

```lean
theorem erdos_418.variants.sigma :
    ∃ (S : Set ℕ) (hS : S.HasPosDensity),
      S ⊆ { (σ 1 n - n : ℕ) | n }ᶜ
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `e0e3cc39f5d40592fe941d670506b65ee60b3d9d5e22575540aab4c2248facb4`)

```lean
:
    ∃ (S : Set ℕ) (hS : S.HasPosDensity),
      S ⊆ { (σ 1 n - n : ℕ) | n }ᶜ
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `2b6af46bd8f8a1259442c0664577191ce05e72d9c0efba7de669379cfa8041cf`)

```text
/--
**Erdős Problem 42**: Let M ≥ 1 and N be sufficiently large in terms of M. Is it true that for every
maximal Sidon set `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` there is another Sidon set `B ⊆ {1,…,N}` of size M such that
`(A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}`?

This was proved for all $M$ by GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Sandhu), see discussion thread for more details.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `60323bfa8a88c8d6da78cc0aaaa5e51350d01b409c63773ced4f68ec22922f54`)

```lean
theorem erdos_42 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ M ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N),
    ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
    ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0}
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `a38f79fa12e5ffbd426f0ce9b314d9d5a2488cbd4d0d99f68ca7d73f6281c5cc`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∀ M ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N),
    ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
    ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0}
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `6a7a157e761df75f64fd96189bc442bdefacd80c302bd5bec3b695c9e3179ab6`)

```text
/--
Is it true that, if $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is sparse enough and does not cover all residue
classes modulo $p$ for any prime $p$, then there exists some $n$ such that $n+a$ is prime for
all $a\in A$?

Weisenberg [We24] has shown the answer is no: $A$ can be arbitrarily sparse and missing at
least one residue class modulo every prime $p$, and yet $A+n$ is not contained in the primes
for any $n\in \mathbb{Z}$. (Weisenberg gives several constructions of such an $A$.)
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `dca78ec2bc1856ae13a52d1b3014cffe7355f6f35c6255ef1826c2d53539495f`)

```lean
theorem erdos_429 : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → (∀ N, (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard ≤ f N) →
        (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ b : ZMod p, ∀ a ∈ A, (a : ZMod p) ≠ b) →
        ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ A, (n + a).Prime
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `849c4491f0497a730af9b29754b8d834126e32dd27553a6fa084e5b7c0463fb2`)

```lean
: answer(False) ↔
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `c67fafb67cc4eca4ed79b6e794389727b8022bfa61a9e58f968964fccce06fe5`)

```text
/--
If $A$ and $B$ are equal-sized Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, can the bound be improved to
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}
    \leq (1-c+o(1))\binom{f(N)}{2}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page records a negative answer due to Barreto.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `06490d0e70c76892bc015b1f0cd6510a47a79dd03802445d06d0055c8341e3e3`)

```lean
theorem erdos_43.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ᵉ (c > 0), ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      A.card = B.card →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        (1 - c + o N) * ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `b26c13e545cbbeaafd8876de856553cfb12377eb3984dc91628edc60c3e1d392`)

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `45ef0f20fff27d381b8272604602980a17ef63d52c92dcd09f58348e5fb59eec`)

```text
/--
Let $\operatorname{Log} x := \max\{\log x, 1\}$,
$\operatorname{Log}_2x = \operatorname{Log} (\operatorname{Log} x)$, and
$\operatorname{Log}_3x = \operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log} x)).$
Is it true that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is such that
$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{Log}_2 x} \sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\to\infty
$$
then
$$
\left(\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\right)^2 \sum_{n, m \in A: n < m \leq x}
\frac{1}{\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)}\to\infty
$$
as $x\to\infty$?

Tao [Ta24b] has shown this is false.

[Ta24b] Tao, T., _Dense sets of natural numbers with unusually large least common multiples_.
arXiv:2407.04226 (2024).

Note: the informal and formal statements follow the solution paper https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04226
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `6562cd827e8ac47bdf8ab3f74f33e6298de26adcdd628df7f9ae3657abbe6d33`)

```lean
theorem erdos_442 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    Tendsto (fun (x : ℝ) =>
      1 / x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne * ∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop →
    Tendsto (fun (x : ℝ) => 1 / (∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) ^ 2 *
      ∑ nm ∈ A.bddProdUpper x, (1 : ℝ) / nm.1.lcm nm.2) atTop atTop
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `138d7c0f40b1b49aa77b6db9a4da329013a374a9fe18ea7cd014f0d4470ce273`)

```lean
: answer(False) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    Tendsto (fun (x : ℝ) =>
      1 / x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne * ∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop →
    Tendsto (fun (x : ℝ) => 1 / (∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) ^ 2 *
      ∑ nm ∈ A.bddProdUpper x, (1 : ℝ) / nm.1.lcm nm.2) atTop atTop
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `b55f754ca12b7717a55157af34d336219465671689b51ba2af3ea5540475959f`)

```text
/--
Let $m,n\geq 1$. What is
$$\# \{ k(m-k) : 1\leq k\leq m/2\} \cap \{ l(n-l) : 1\leq l\leq n/2\}?$$
Can it be arbitrarily large?

This was solved independently by Hegyvári [He25] and Cambie (unpublished), who show that if
$m>n$ then the set in question has size
$$\leq m^{O(1/\log\log m)},$$
and that for any integer $s$ there exist infinitely many pairs $(m,n)$ such that the set in
question has size $s$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `34340bfe81e0004109027c2b094afe08ba7cf23f23ab0df58a3fa8fb8c907efb`)

```lean
theorem erdos_443.parts.i : answer(True) ↔

```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `8579e335231b01aa88f6e6432be9f89028ba8b3bc595f89c9e449248e99f747a`)

```text
/--
Let $m,n\geq 1$. What is
$$\# \{ k(m-k) : 1\leq k\leq m/2\} \cap \{ l(n-l) : 1\leq l\leq n/2\}?$$
Is it $\leq (mn)^{o(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $m,n$?

This was solved independently by Hegyvári [He25] and Cambie (unpublished), who show that if
$m>n$ then the set in question has size
$$\leq m^{O(1/\log\log m)},$$
and that for any integer $s$ there exist infinitely many pairs $(m,n)$ such that the set in
question has size $s$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `4f457c2eb8b2cf20edafe3d1011aed886f13477163484b024a879e1ed6224d51`)

```lean
theorem erdos_443.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ m n : ℕ, n₀ < n → n < m →
      ((A n ∩ A m).card : ℝ) < ((m : ℝ) * n) ^ ε
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `5bfed42cd195b3b9c01a6bc5324a3984c0096dab695738bf88d8fc1a501fbdf9`)

```lean
: answer(True) ↔
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ m n : ℕ, n₀ < n → n < m →
      ((A n ∩ A m).card : ℝ) < ((m : ℝ) * n) ^ ε
```

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `5fe5e041b9a6655ac79eac18f371261d046701878b8ce17d36d2410eec40b2e2`)

```text
/--
How large can a union-free collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ be? By union-free we mean
there are no solutions to $A\cup B=C$ with distinct $A,B,C\in \mathcal{F}$. Must
$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert =o(2^n)$?

In [Er65b] Erdős reported that the estimate $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=o(2^n)$ was proved in
unpublished work by Sárközy and Szemerédi.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `8ab65dc2b2cfa170bd8f480f53026bd4a7ba6af95f22fcd0e3e9ee8ac9fff95e`)

```lean
theorem erdos_447.parts.i : answer(True) ↔
    (fun n : ℕ => (maxUnionFree n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n)
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `254d325fce1661ab6578061b4bc929e548010f1b232db9e6eb31a44c6caf0385`)

```lean

    (fun n : ℕ => (maxUnionFree n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n)
```

```text
/--

```

```text
/--
A translate-uniform **linear** scale suffices: there is a sufficient window
length `Y` with `Y ε n ≤ C(ε) · n`. This is an upper bound on the optimal scale,
not the exact threshold asked for in `erdos_450`.
-/
```

```lean
theorem erdos_450.linear_scale_suffices :

```

```lean
    liminf (fun n : ℕ => (q n : ℝ≥0∞) / n ^ 2) atTop > 0.352
```

### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `4f24d830cc41962c35a353781d3c82722cc201ca25dd2f06ee7a3ae3a2672d01`)

```text
/--
Let $f(u)$ be the largest $v$ such that no $m\in (u,v)$ is composed entirely of primes dividing
$uv$. Estimate $f(u)$.

The estimate $u + 2 \le f(u) \le u^2$ holds for every $u \ge 2$. The upper bound is attained
when $u$ is prime, and the lower bound when $u = 2^k - 2$ with $k \ge 2$; Cambie further showed
that $f(n) = (1 + o(1))n$ for almost all $n$.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `9965db39bc926943a9792ce2a94cc2735f88c2e9ceb751cae8aa9a4a0ed689bc`)

```lean
theorem erdos_459 {u : ℕ} (hu : 2 ≤ u) : u + 2 ≤ f u ∧ f u ≤ u ^ 2
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `741e9cc144bcb18e17d165d525cddcedfc63d9e69ab3bede42b7da63a8ff91f2`)


### 精确陈述 / Exact statement

#### 源文档字符串 / Source docstring (SHA-256 `6a2927c8501570d1630e669e059b117d2b829d60c719abf7dd821976f9373246`)

```text
/--
Does every finite colouring of the integers have a monochromatic solution to
$1=\sum \frac{1}{n_i}$ with $2\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$?

The answer is yes, as proved by Croot [Cr03] - indeed, there are infinitely many disjoint such
monochromatic solutions.
-/
```

#### Lean 声明 / Lean declaration (SHA-256 `7a64d5f8b84f73fd99111453f2c98c5aafeb5f50bef7ce8547623187088db778`)

```lean
theorem erdos_46 :
    answer(True) ↔
    -- For any finite colouring of the integers
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℕ → ℕ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      -- there are integers `2 ≤ n₁ < ⋯ < n_k`
      ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 2 ≤ n) ∧
        -- whose reciprocals sum to `1`
        ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1 ∧
        -- and which all have the same colour
        (𝓒 '' (S : Set ℕ)).Subsingleton
```

#### 精确声明类型 / Exact declaration type (SHA-256 `889335c77305cc2233253e70b71c4b4cdc8c1404a9016de5cb7ed9e886b1d5dc`)

```lean
:
    answer(True) ↔
    -- For any finite colouring of the integers
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℕ → ℕ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      -- there are integers `2 ≤ n₁ < ⋯ < n_k`
      ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 2 ≤ n) ∧
        -- whose reciprocals sum to `1`
        ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1 ∧
        -- and which all have the same colour
        (𝓒 '' (S : Set ℕ)).Subsingleton
```
